summary.text: Island formation covers the ways a piece of land, separate from a continent and surrounded by water, comes into being.
Continental islands split off from a continent through plate tectonics, while oceanic islands, never part of a continent, build up from volcanoes, coral reefs or shoreline sediment.
Where a plate slides over a fixed volcanic hotspot, it leaves a line of islands that grow older and more worn down the farther they sit from the hotspot.

facts.label: Line Islands age
facts.value: All estimated at 8 million years old

facts.label: Zealandia submerged
facts.value: An estimated 93% of its original area

items.prompt: In a chain of volcanic islands made by a plate moving over a hotspot, you visit the island farthest from the hotspot. What should you expect?

options.label: It is the youngest and tallest of the chain
It is the oldest and most worn down
It is the most active volcano of the chain
It is the same age as all the others

items.explain: The plate carries islands away from the fixed hotspot, so the farther ones are progressively older and more eroded before they sink.

items.prompt: Scientists date every island in one chain and find they all formed at about the same time. What does that suggest?

options.label: A plate slowly drifted over a single hotspot
Coral built each island one after another
Cracks in the plate made them all at once
Rivers dropped sediment to build each one

items.explain: Some chains form all at once from fractures in the plate itself; the Line Islands, all about 8 million years old, support this.

items.prompt: An island's plants and animals closely match those on a nearby mainland. Which kind of island is it most likely to be?

options.label: A volcanic oceanic island
A coral atoll
A barrier island of sand
A continental island

items.explain: Continental islands split from a continent and so share their plant and animal life with it, while oceanic islands were never part of one.

items.prompt: A volcanic island slowly sinks, but the coral reef around it keeps growing. What can this eventually produce?

options.label: An atoll ringing a central lagoon
A barrier island of sand
A new continental island
A chain of hotspot volcanoes

items.explain: Coral reefs growing on submerged volcanic islands form islands, and when these coral islands encircle a central lagoon the result is an atoll.

items.prompt: New Zealand sits on Zealandia, a continent-like piece of crust. Roughly how much of Zealandia's original surface is thought to be under the sea?

options.label: About 10%
About 35%
About 60%
About 93%

items.explain: An estimated 93% of Zealandia's original surface area has been submerged, leaving islands like New Zealand as what remains.

items.prompt: Why do plants and animals on an oceanic island often end up unlike those anywhere else?

options.label: The sea limits new arrivals, so they evolve in isolation
Volcanic soil changes their genes directly
They are left over from the continent nearby
Ice joins the island to the mainland in winter

items.explain: The sea acts as a barrier to new species, so the species that do arrive evolve in isolation.
